Article Title: Identity of 'Dimagi Naxal Party' founder remains a mystery
Article Text:
One Insta post states, "When someone says Dimaagi Naxal, all I hear is intellectual baddie!'

What's common to the social media accounts of 'Dimagi Naxal Party' - started over the weekend in response to PM's reference in his I-Day speech - and CJP protests is a high dose of Gen Z humour.One Insta post states, "When someone says Dimaagi Naxal, all I hear is intellectual baddie!'Its X handle @DNJP_India has amassed 14,000 followers, while a handful of X accounts have also added 'dimagi Naxal' as a prefix to their names as an act of solidarity. There's also a website with a manifesto and an anthem - which links to a YouTube clip from the 2006 Hindi film 'Rang De Basanti' featuring the actors reciting the revolutionary poem 'Sarfaroshi Ki Tamanna'.Following PM's remarks, Congress' P Chidambaram called himself a 'proud dimagi Naxal' in a post on X, while actor Prakash Raj posted a reel urging people to become 'dimaagi' and not 'bewakoof'. Union minister Kiren Rijiju clarified that the term was not directed at opposition, and even came out with a three-point definition of who qualifies as a dimagi Naxal: those who support Maoists and reject Constitution, those who stand with separatists and support Article 370, and those who want to cut the chicken neck to separate the Northeast from India.While the identity of its founder (who is simply going by the name 'a dimagi Indian' online) has not yet been publicly disclosed, DNJP calls CJP a sibling party on its website. Its first tweet Sunday, "What if all dimagi naxals come together?" was also a hat tip to CJP's origin, which began with Abhijeet Dipke's now-iconic May 16 tweet, "What if all the cockroaches come together?"Unlike CJP, however, DNJP's 'manifesto' states that there will be no flag, no font, or founder doing press, and the only criteria for joining the party is a "functioning brain and a willingness to ask 'wait, why though' out loud". It is also clear about one thing: the deployment of terms such as 'dimagi Naxals' and 'anti-nationals' crosses party lines and is often used to shut down criticism."Every side of Indian politics has, at some point, called the other side 'anti-national' for disagreeing," the website says. "DNJP's bet: the people who actually think for themselves are scattered across every one of those parties - and a label meant to isolate them is exactly what could bring them back together."
Article Summary: 'Dimagi Naxal Party' started over the weekend in response to PM's reference in his I-Day speech. Its X handle @DNJP_India has amassed 14,000 followers, while a handful of X accounts have also added 'dimagi' as a prefix to their names as an act of solidarity.

NEW DELHI: India's star wicketkeeper batter Rishabh Pant created history on Tuesday during the first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle. The India wicketkeeper-batter became the first Indian cricketer to hit 100 sixes in Test cricket.Pant reached the milestone with a big six off Lahiru Kumara. The shot also brought up his 20th Test fifty.Pant became only the fourth batter in Test history to hit 100 sixes. Ben Stokes leads the list with 138 sixes, followed by Brendon McCullum with 107. Pant is now third with 100 sixes, while former Australia wicketkeeper Adam Gilchrist also has 100.Pant reached the landmark in his aggressive style against Kumara. The Sri Lankan pacer bowled a delivery on a length and angled it into the left-hander. Pant got inside the line and pulled it over long leg.Nuwantha tried to catch the ball but could only watch it sail over the boundary.The six also brought up Pant's fifty, his 20th in Test cricket.With the shot, Pant became the first Indian and only the fourth batter overall to reach 100 sixes in Test cricket.
Article Summary: Rishabh Pant becomes the first Indian cricketer to hit 100 sixes in Test cricket. Pant reached the milestone with a big six off Lahiru Kumara. The shot also brought up his 20th Test fifty. Ben Stokes leads the list with 138 sixes, followed by Brendon McCullum with 107.

Article Title: BJP puts Vinod Tawde, who played role in Bihar win, in charge of UP
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: BJP Tuesday appointed Vinod Tawde , who was involved in its winning campaign in Bihar last year, as its state in-charge for Uttar Pradesh, the politically critical state which goes to the polls early next year, as it begins putting in place its team ahead of the next round of crucial contests.BJP made a series of appointments a day after its president, Nitin Nabin, announced the party's new team of national office-bearers, with MP Satish Poonia given charge of Punjab, another poll-bound state, and MP Tarun Chugh of Gujarat.Tawde was being tipped for UP and the decision, when formally announced, marked his steady rise in the party's national organisation, into which he was absorbed in 2020 following a period of uncertainty since being denied a ticket to contest the Maharashtra assembly poll in 2019.He was taken aboard as a national secretary and then elevated as a general secretary in 2021, a position he has retained in the new team. He has often served as a coordinator on key organisational issues and was in charge of Bihar in 2025 in a poll that NDA won empathically. Jagdish Ishwarbhai Patel, a secretary, has been made co-incharge of UP.MP Tawde, a Maratha, is now in charge of two key heartland Hindi states as BJP looks to retain office for a third straight term in UP. It is also a state where relations between the party's organisational machinery and govt led by CM Yogi Adityanath have been on an ev-en keel, making his role as the link between the two crucial.Poonia, a Jat and former Rajasthan BJP president, gets charge of Punjab at a time when the revival of the party's alliance with Akali Dal is being seen as a possibility after the regional party's president, Sukhbir Singh Badal, met PM Narendra Modi and announced his support for the delimitation bill that seeks to increase Lok Sabha's strength.
Article Summary: Vinod Tawde, who was involved in winning campaign in Bihar, appointed state in- charge for Uttar Pradesh. Satish Poonia given charge of Punjab, another poll- bound state, and MP Tarun Chugh of Gujarat. Jagdish Ishwarbhai Patel, a secretary, has been made co-incharge of UP.

Article Title: Ritabrata Banerjee to remain Bengal LoP till decision on plea within 2 months, says HC
Article Text:
Ritabrata Banerjee to continue as the LoP in the West Bengal Assembly.

NEW DELHI: Ritabrata Banerjee will continue as the leader of opposition in the West Bengal Assembly for now as the Calcutta high court division bench on Tuesday declined to disturb his appointment at the current stage.The bench of Justices Shampa Sarkar and Ajay Kumar Gupta directed that the challenge to his appointment be decided by a single judge within two months.The case was filed by Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay, a TMC MLA from the Mamata Banerjee camp, who had challenged assembly speaker Rathindra Bose's decision to appoint Ritabrata Banerjee as the leader of opposition.The division bench's order means that Banerjee will remain in the post until the single bench decides Chattopadhyay's petition.Chattopadhyay had approached the high court after the Speaker rejected his claim to the post and appointed Ritabrata Banerjee instead.The matter had earlier come before a single bench, which on June 18 declined to grant any interim relief against the speaker's decision. Chattopadhyay then challenged that order before the division bench.The division bench has now directed the single bench to hear the challenge to the speaker's decision and reach a decision within two months.Until then, Ritabrata Banerjee will continue as leader of opposition.Ritabrata, Sandipan Saha (who is now deputy LoP), and several other rebel MLAs backing BJP-led NDA have alleged their signatures were forged on a May 6 letter sent to the assembly speaker proposing Sobhandeb's name as LoP - a case making headlines as "signgate" and being investigated by Bengal police CID.Sandipan called high court's refusal to intervene a "moral victory". "Ritabrata and I had initiated this fight. We brought the alleged signature irregularities in TMC's letter to the speaker's notice. The issue then went to court. Today's victory in HC confirms that law is on our side," he said.High court's refusal to hit pause has left Ritabrata firmly in the saddle for now, but courtroom battles and political trench warfare inside TMC show few signs of easing. "Of 80 Trinamool MLAs, 65 are with us. Of the remaining 15, one is in jail. For the time being, 14 are on the other side. Let us wait and watch," Ritabrata said.
Article Summary: Ritabrata Banerjee will continue as the leader of opposition in the West Bengal Assembly. Calcutta high court division bench declined to disturb his appointment at the current stage. Justices Shampa Sarkar and Ajay Kumar Gupta directed that the challenge to his appointment be decided by a single judge within two months. The case was filed by Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay, a TMC MLA.

Article Title: Nitin's 'Nabin' team: BJP hits reset button with eye on Uttar Pradesh and 'Mission 2029'
Article Text:
Both Ram Madhav and Smriti Irani secured key positions in the BJP, while Amit Malviya was dropped from the new team.

Here are some highlights of Nitin's 'Nabin' team

The overhauled national team has 51 new office-bearers out of the 65 names announced, signalling a significant break from the past.

The new team has widespread representation, accommodating voices from 23 states and Union territories across the country.

Every major faith is respected and accommodated. The national team has one Sikh member, two Christian members and one member each from Muslim, Jain and Parsi communities.

The youngest BJP chief has opted for a relatively young team. Six office-bearers are below 40 years, 15 are in the 40-49 years age group, and 21 are in the 50-59 years age group.

The committee has four tribal representatives from West Bengal, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and the North-East, two of whom are women.

Special focus has been placed on the northeast region, with three regional leaders from Tripura, Assam and Nagaland and the continuation of a dedicated North-East Coordination Cell.

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Monday hit the reset button as party president Nitin Nabin announced a new national team of office-bearers to prepare the party for the upcoming round of assembly elections, leading up to the 2029 Lok Sabha challenge. The party leaders described the newly constituted team as a strategic blend of seasoned administrative and organisational experience, youthfulness, geographic diversity and comprehensive social inclusion.The list has some high-profile omissions and some surprise comebacks. While Amit Malviya did not find a place in the new team after serving as BJP’s I-T cell head for 11 years, Ram Madhav and Smriti Irani made a grand comeback after staying on the fringes for long.Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated the newly appointed national office-bearers. "Congratulations to the newly appointed national office bearers of the BJP and those who have been given various responsibilities in the party. This newly appointed team brings together organisational experience, energy and grassroots connect," PM Modi said on X.BJP chief Nitin Nabin called his team a blend of experience and energy that will provide new momentum to the organisation and take forward PM Modi’s vision of 'Viksit Bharat'.In a post on X, Nabin said, "Heartiest congratulations and best wishes to all the newly appointed office-bearers of the Bharatiya Janata Party's National Team. With a blend of experience and energy, this team will give new momentum to the organisation under the guidance of Hon'ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi.""I am confident that every member, with the spirit of a dedicated karyakarta, will further strengthen the organisation to take forward the resolve of a 'Viksit Bharat' and the commitment to nation-building to new heights," he further said."Such balanced appointments empower the incoming national president's executive team to operate with a profound awareness of the nation's vast geographical landscape and regional nuances," the BJP said in a statement.Uttar Pradesh, which goes to polls early next year, has been the biggest focus in this BJP reset. As many as 8 leaders from Uttar Pradesh have found a place in Nitin Nabin's team, the most notable being Smriti Irani, who once defeated Rahul Gandhi from his bastion Amethi Lok Sabha seat.Among national vice-presidents, Rekha Verma and Prof Tariq Mansoor are from UP. Smriti Irani and Harish Dwivedi have been appointed national general secretaries.Two national secretaries and two Morcha presidents are also from UP.BJP’s new national team marks the comeback of several leaders who were on the sidelines in recent times. From former Union minister Smriti Irani and RSS veteran Ram Madhav to former chief ministers Biplab Kumar Deb and Tirath Singh Rawat, several BJP leaders who had either slipped out of the party's top organisational structure or seen their political stock diminish have returned to prominent roles in the new national team.Smriti Irani, whose biggest claim to fame is her victory over Rahul Gandhi in 2019 Lok Sabha elections in Amethi, ending the Gandhi family's decades-long dominance over the constituency, thanked PM Modi and BJP president Nitin Nabin for reposing their faith in her and said she would work to strengthen the organisation at the grassroots while contributing to the party's vision of a "Viksit Bharat."She described her political journey from an "ordinary BJP karyakarta" to one of the party's top organisational posts as "deeply humbling." She thanked PM Modi and BJP president Nitin Nabin for reposing their faith in her and said she would work to strengthen the organisation at the grassroots while contributing to the party's vision of a "Viksit Bharat."The return of Ram Madhav, who has been made a national vice-president, is also significant.A former RSS spokesperson who was deputed to the BJP in 2014, Madhav emerged as one of the party's most influential general secretaries during its first term in power under PM Modi. He played a key role in the BJP's expansion in the northeast and was one of the principal architects of its alliance with the PDP in Jammu and Kashmir after the 2014 assembly polls.His influence waned after the BJP-PDP government collapsed in 2018, and he was dropped as a national general secretary when then BJP president J P Nadda constituted his team in September 2020. He subsequently largely disappeared from the BJP's organisational front line.The BJP later brought him back to oversee its Jammu and Kashmir assembly election campaign along with Union minister G Kishan Reddy in 2024.The first meeting of the Nitin Nabin's new team is scheduled to be held on August 22, news agency ANI reported citing government sources. However, its first test will be in early 2027 when several states, including Uttar Pradesh and Punjab, go to the polls. The BJP has a duanting task at hand in Uttar Pradesh, where the Samajwadi Party and the Congress together pushed it on the backfoot in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.Meanwhile, with changes in the party structure announced, all eyes would now be on the possible changed in the Union Cabinet.
Article Summary: BJP president Nitin Nabin announced a new national team of office-bearers on Monday. The overhauled national team has 51 new office- bearers out of the 65 names announced. The list has some high-profile omissions and some surprise comebacks. Ram Madhav and Smriti Irani secured key positions in the new team.

Article Title: “I had the ability to forgive”: How Baker Mayfield chose forgiveness to reopen the door with his family after $11.741M dispute
Article Text:
How Baker Mayfield chose forgiveness to reopen the door with his family after $11.741M dispute(Getty Images)

How did Baker Mayfield choose forgiveness after the $11.741 million family dispute?

How did Kova help Baker Mayfield rebuild his family relationship?

Baker Mayfield has found a way forward in one of the hardest chapters of his life. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback is rebuilding ties with his family after a financial dispute involving $11.741 million. His daughter Kova helped create a new opening. Now, Mayfield says forgiveness has allowed him to look beyond a painful family fight and focus on what comes next.The dispute dates back to 2018, when money belonging to Baker Mayfield, Emily Mayfield and their company allegedly moved to businesses connected to Baker’s father and brother. The case later reached court before Mayfield sought a different path with his family.The conflict began between 2018 and 2021, when Baker Mayfield and Emily Mayfield alleged that about $12 million from their accounts and Team BRM moved to companies connected to Baker Mayfield’s father, James W. Mayfield, and brother, Matt Mayfield. The Mayfields claimed they did not authorize the transfers and did not receive an equity interest in the company.The issue became more serious in August 2023, when Baker Mayfield and Emily Mayfield sought financial records connected to the companies.The two sides later reached a confidential settlement that became effective on January 23, 2024. Under that agreement, Camwood Capital agreed to repay $11.741 million plus interest.But the settlement did not close the chapter. On Nov. 22, 2024, Baker Mayfield, Emily Mayfield and Team BRM filed another lawsuit. They alleged that Camwood Capital had not made the required payments or fulfilled other terms of the settlement.That history makes Baker Mayfield’s latest comments much more meaningful. Despite everything that happened, the Buccaneers quarterback has decided not to let the dispute permanently define his relationship with his family.In an interview with the Tampa Bay Times, Baker Mayfield explained how his daughter Kova helped change the situation. He recalled taking Kova to meet his family around her first birthday and described the emotional effect of that meeting.“It's been good. Also, for them to have two grandbabies, it's tough. What's in the past is in the past. Emily and I took (daughter Kova) down right around her first birthday. First time they met her, and you (could) tell it just melted them.He further added, “You can't put yourself on a pedestal and act like I haven't made mistakes in my life. I had the ability to forgive and that was what I wanted to get across. But we're here, and the door is open.”The quote explains the change better than any legal document could. Baker Mayfield did not say the dispute never happened. Instead, he accepted that the past existed while choosing to make room for his family again.Kova’s meeting with Baker Mayfield’s family gave everyone something new to focus on. Mayfield said having two grandchildren made the situation harder to keep apart, especially after the family finally met his daughter.That moment also gave Baker Mayfield a chance to approach the relationship differently. He acknowledged his own mistakes and chose forgiveness instead of continuing the conflict.For the Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback, that does not erase the $11.741 million legal battle. It simply separates the financial dispute from his hopes for his family.The legal fight may remain part of Baker Mayfield’s history, but his latest comments show that he does not want it to control his family’s future. His message is clear: the past stays in the past, while the door to reconciliation remains open.
Article Summary: Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback is rebuilding ties with his family after a financial dispute involving $11.741 million. The dispute dates back to 2018, when money belonging to Baker Mayfield, Emily Mayfield and their company allegedly moved to businesses connected to Baker’s father and brother. The two sides later reached a confidential settlement that became effective on January 23, 2024.

Article Title: Patrick Mahomes’ wife Brittany Mahomes shares family picture but covers her own face with a big white heart emoji – is the NFL WAG hiding a makeup free look?
Article Text:

Patrick Mahomes’ wife Brittany Mahomes covers her face with a white heart

Some lines from Paris Paloma’s famous 2023 song “Labour” read:“All day every day, therapist, mother maid,” “Just an appendage, live to attend him,”“24/7 baby machine so he can live out his picket-fence dreams,” and “it’s not an act of love if you make her… you make me do too much labour.”Now, the song reference here may be over the top [obviously!] But the point is that women can sometimes feel they have to go through too much “labour” after marriage. The husband. The kids. Their everything.So, when Patrick Mahomes ’ wife, Brittany Mahomes , shared a lovely, homely snapshot of her family of five on Instagram , she covered her own beautiful face with a big white heart. Why? Several reasons could explain it.“Too much labour” could have caused dark circles. “Too much labour” could have caused facial puffiness. “Too much labour” could have brought on wrinkles.These “wrinkles,” “dark circles,” and “facial puffiness” are all normal signs that can come with age and everyday life.But if they get out to the world, if the world sees the Kansas City Chiefs star quarterback’s wife with all those “normal” things… well, it could invite unwanted scrutiny. Better safe than sorry!So, Brittany Mahomes covers her face with a big white heart.Perhaps she doesn’t want to become a meme fest or face social-media scrutiny and internet sleuthing over whether she has “dark circles,” “facial puffiness,” “facial acne,” “acne scars,” or “wrinkles,” if any.To top it off, imagine the thought-process she might have had before adding that big white heart to her sleepy, tired, or makeup-free face?Underconfident? Personal privacy? Or just plain, “I do not want to share my non-makeup face with the world”?The “white heart over face” comes as a surprise because Patrick Mahomes has often spoken highly of Brittany’s confidence.“Whether it’s in business, or supporting our family, she always leads with strength and purpose. That kind of confidence is powerful; it pushes me to be better every day,” Mahomes told PEOPLE in June 2025.“Confidence isn’t something that you just wake up with one day. It’s about staying committed to our goals, trusting yourself and the people around you and putting your best foot forward with every opportunity you get.”Now this Patrick’s revelation makes Brittany’s decision to cover her face in the latest Instagram Story contradicting, especially when Brittany has previously spoken openly about her skin struggles and shared makeup-free selfies.Brittany previously got candid about her skincare. The wife of three-time Super Bowl champion took to her Instagram Story in March 2024 to share a selfie video about some of the struggles she had been dealing with when it came to acne on her face.“Okay, I’m not really sure if anyone wants to hear this, but I feel like I need to share my skin series with you guys because I have been trying to figure out for so long,” Brittany said.“And it’ll randomly just flare up, and then it’ll start to get better, and then it’ll randomly just go wild again. And last night, it was literally like hives and red, like, all down here around my mouth, so I have no idea what’s causing it.I feel like I’ve changed everything that I use, and I have no idea. So, if anyone does know or has recommendations, please let me know.”
Article Summary: Patrick Mahomes’ wife, Brittany Mahomes, shared a lovely, homely snapshot of her family of five on Instagram. She covered her own beautiful face with a big white heart. The “white heart over face” comes as a surprise because Patrick Mahomes has often spoken highly of Brittany's confidence.

Article Title: “We want your pee, please give us your pee": Why Jason Kelce singing about urine in a meadow is actually the smartest marketing campaign of 2026
Article Text:
Jason Kelce "we want you pee" ad (Getty Images)

What exactly is Jason Kelce asking fans to do in the Garage Beer and Liquid Death campaign?

Why is Jason Kelce the face of Garage Beer and how big is the brand now?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jason Kelce has made some memorable moments since retiring from the NFL, but nothing quite prepared the internet for this one. On Tuesday, August 18, the former Philadelphia Eagles center and Garage Beer co-owner appeared in a new joint campaign with Liquid Death, asking fans to do something most brands would never dare request: send in their urine. Not as a prank. Not as a stunt with no point. Kelce and the brands are dead serious about the cause -- AI data centers across the United States are consuming up to 5 million gallons of water per day to cool their servers, and they want you to help fix it. With your pee.The ad opens with Jason Kelce sitting on a toilet, filling up a jar, and explaining the problem directly to the camera: *"AI data centers waste millions of gallons of water. That's why Liquid Death and Garage Beer decided to team up: We want your pee … to cool these data centers."*It only gets stranger from there. Kelce steps outside into an open meadow, joins Liquid Death's mascot Murder Man, and breaks into song. The chorus, which has already lodged itself into the brains of anyone who has seen the ad, goes: "We want your pee, please give us your pee. Let's pee on computers together. 'Cause we need lots of pee, endless gallons of pee.Join our important endeavor. We want your pee, please give us your pee. Let's pee on computers together to save humanity, we want your pee."The campaign, titled "We Want Your Pee," is framed as a P[EE].S.A. -- a public service announcement with a very specific twist. It is built around a real statistic: there are more than 4,000 data centers operating in the United States, and each one can consume up to 5 million gallons of water daily. Human urine, according to the Cleveland Clinic, is between 91 and 96 percent water. Humans produce anywhere from three to eight cups per day. The math, at least in concept, is right there.The campaign will run with paid support across Garage Beer and Liquid Death's social channels and on connected TV, with a limited "Coolant Collector" product also being sold as part of the launch.Kelce, 38, and his brother Travis Kelce became co-owners of Garage Beer in June 2024, purchasing a majority stake and taking the largest investor positions in the company. This was not a passive celebrity endorsement deal. Garage Beer CEO Andy Sauer told the Wall Street Journal that the Kelce brothers are genuinely hands-on in how the brand operates."It's pretty emblematic on how they both operate," Sauer said. "It's an always-on relationship. It's two people with the same vision and belief in beer, jumping into it."The brand itself is an American-style light craft lager at 95 calories, launched in 2023. By September 2025, it had been valued at $200 million. When Jason signed on, he was clear about why it appealed to him: "People crave quality and simplicity, and Garage Beer nails both for me. We are light beer drinkers and Garage is the best light beer. For me, the brand fits my lifestyle, and having a few beers is a great excuse to get the neighbors together.Travis echoed that energy: "I think everyone knows I like to have a couple beers now and then, so being an owner of Garage Beer and heavily involved in making the best light beer is exciting, man! There is nothing better to bring people together than an ice-cold beer, and for Jason and me that is what beer is all about -- friends, family and fun."Outside Garage Beer, Jason owns Underdog Apparel and has collaborated with Homage on merchandise tied to the "New Heights" podcast he runs with Travis. He has done ad work for Buffalo Wild Wings, Campbell's, and Bazooka Candy Brands over the years. But this one is different. This campaign is not about moving product through a 30-second spot. It is about tapping into a real public tension around AI, water usage, and Big Tech — and doing it in the most Jason Kelce way possible: loud, weird, and oddly earnest.

Article Title: ‘Ball was on the ground’: Ex-cricketer baffled as Dhruv Jurel catch sparks controversy

India moved within touching distance of victory in the Galle Test on Tuesday, making repeated breakthroughs in Sri Lanka's batting order to leave themselves needing six more wickets on the final day to take a 1-0 lead in the two-match series.But the fourth day's play was overshadowed by a contentious third-umpire decision involving wicketkeeper Dhruv Jurel, whose catch to dismiss Sri Lanka opener Lahiru Udara triggered debate among fans and commentators.The incident took place on the fourth ball of the 22nd over, with Manav Suthar bowling. Jurel completed the catch, but Udara immediately appeared unsure whether the ball had been taken cleanly. The matter was referred to third umpire Raveendra Wimalasiri, with replays showing the ball going into Jurel's hands but leaving some doubt over whether his fingers were underneath it.Jurel had held the ball with his right hand and, as his momentum carried him forward, there appeared to be a possibility that the ball had made contact with the ground. Wimalasiri, however, was satisfied with the available evidence and ruled Udara out.Udara was visibly unhappy with the decision and appeared reluctant to leave the field. The Sri Lankan opener had made 16 off 58 balls before being forced to walk back to the pavilion.Former Sri Lanka batter Russel Arnold , who was part of the commentary team, was also not convinced that the catch was clean. He felt the ball had touched the ground and believed Udara should have remained at the crease.“It's been pushed along the ground for a bit. The ball was pushed along the ground. You can see, it was pushed along. When you look at that slow-motion replay, it seems that the fingers were pushed back and the front of the ball was touching the ground,” Arnold said on air.“For me, the ball is on the ground there. The fingers are behind the ball,” he added.India had set Sri Lanka a target of 372 after being dismissed for 193 in their second innings. Rishabh Pant top-scored with 66 and also became the first Asian batter to cross 100 sixes in Test cricket.Sri Lanka struggled during their chase as India picked up four wickets before stumps. Suthar claimed two, while Mohammed Siraj and Prasidh Krishna took one each.The hosts finished the fourth day on 84/4 and still require 288 runs to pull off a remarkable victory. With rain forecast for the final day, India will have to negotiate the weather as they look to complete a 1-0 series lead in Galle.
Article Summary: Wicketkeeper Dhruv Jurel's catch to dismiss Sri Lanka opener Lahiru Udara triggered debate among fans and commentators. The incident took place on the fourth ball of the 22nd over, with Manav Suthar bowling. Udara appeared unsure whether the ball had been taken cleanly. The matter was referred to third umpire Raveendra Wimalasiri, who ruled Udara out.

Article Title: Jamal Musiala’s 'absence seizures' explained: What causes them, what happens during episodes and how dangerous they are
Article Text:
Jamal Musiala’s absence seizures explained: What causes them, what happens during episodes and how dangerous they are.

What are absence seizures ?

Why can someone appear to collapse during an episode?

What causes absence seizures?

How concerning is it for Musiala to have an episode while playing football?

What happened to Musiala before this?

What has Musiala said about his future?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jamal Musiala has revealed that he has been diagnosed with “temporarily occurring, brief absence seizures” after collapsing during two Bayern Munich friendlies within four days. The 23-year-old Germany international said the episodes are caused by a neurological dysfunction, are treatable and are currently being managed with specialist medical care.The disclosure came after Musiala collapsed during Tuesday’s 4-2 friendly win over Heidenheim, just days after a similar episode against RB Leipzig. He has since said that he is doing well, remains optimistic and, after consultation with neurological specialists, intends to continue living normally and pursuing his career in football.Absence seizures involve brief, sudden lapses in consciousness. They are much more common in children than adults and can sometimes be mistaken for a person simply losing concentration or staring into space.According to the Mayo Clinic , a simple absence seizure typically lasts about 10 seconds, although it can last as long as 30 seconds. During an episode, the person may suddenly stop what they are doing and stare blankly into space before quickly returning to an alert state. Massachusetts General Hospital describes the loss of awareness as usually lasting between five and 30 seconds. A person experiencing one may appear to be daydreaming and may not respond normally to what is happening around them.There is generally no confusion, headache or drowsiness after a typical absence seizure, and the person may have no memory of the episode. If episodes happen repeatedly, however, they can interfere with everyday activities. Small movements such as eyelid fluttering, lip smacking, chewing motions or finger rubbing can also occur, according to the Mayo Clinic and Massachusetts General Hospital.A typical absence seizure does not usually involve the dramatic muscle jerking associated with some other seizure types, and people generally recover quickly without the confusion, headache or drowsiness that can follow other seizures.That distinction matters when considering what has been seen with Musiala. The Bayern midfielder has appeared disoriented and collapsed during matches, but his public statement does not provide enough medical detail to determine precisely how his individual episodes present beyond the diagnosis he disclosed.An absence seizure is fundamentally a temporary interruption of awareness rather than the kind of prolonged loss of consciousness that people may associate with a conventional faint.That distinction is relevant to what happened with Musiala. During both Bayern matches, he appeared disoriented before going down, with the incidents occurring while he was actively playing.Against RB Leipzig on Saturday, August 15, Musiala appeared unsteady before beginning to fall. New Bayern team-mate Ismael Saibari reacted immediately, catching him and helping lower him safely to the ground before medical staff attended to him.Musiala was able to leave the pitch under his own power and subsequently returned to training.Four days later, he came off the bench against Heidenheim and suffered another episode. Players from both teams surrounded him as medical staff came onto the pitch, before he was helped away from the playing area.The repeated nature of the incidents prompted understandable concern, but Musiala subsequently explained that both episodes were connected to the diagnosis he had received.Absence seizures occur because of abnormal electrical activity in the brain, temporarily disrupting normal awareness.The condition is particularly associated with childhood. The Mayo Clinic says absence seizures are more common in children, while Massachusetts General Hospital notes that they can begin in childhood, most commonly between the ages of 8 and 15, although some people continue experiencing them into adulthood.Some episodes can also be triggered by factors such as flashing lights or rapid, deep breathing, according to the medical information provided by Massachusetts General Hospital.There is no information from Musiala indicating what specifically triggered either of his recent episodes, and he has asked for the details of his condition to remain private.An absence seizure itself is generally brief and does not usually cause physical injury. The Mayo Clinic notes, however, that the circumstances in which one occurs can create risks. A sudden lapse in awareness while driving, cycling or performing another activity where continuous attention is required can result in injury.For an elite footballer, the question is therefore not simply whether an absence seizure is usually physically damaging. A temporary loss of awareness while running, challenging for the ball or moving at speed can create an entirely different set of risks.Musiala has specifically addressed that concern himself. He said that, in his case, “there is no additional health risk beyond this” and that, after consultation with neurological specialists, he had been cleared to continue his normal life and pursue football.He also said he was receiving the best possible medical care and remained “very optimistic,” according to his statement.The latest diagnosis comes after several difficult seasons from an injury perspective.Musiala suffered a serious ankle injury during the 2025 FIFA Club World Cup following a challenge involving then-Paris Saint-Germain goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma. The injury kept him out for several months, with his return coming in the second half of the following season.He subsequently dealt with further ankle problems that disrupted his recovery and limited his ability to regain his best form. He nevertheless returned to the Germany squad for the 2026 World Cup and started three of the country's four matches at the tournament.The two recent Bayern incidents are therefore separate from that injury history and concern a neurological condition that Musiala has only now publicly identified.Musiala also sought to reassure supporters about what comes next, saying he remains optimistic about his recovery and feels well supported by Bayern Munich and those around him. “I know they might look scary at first glance, but for me, they are currently just part of my everyday life,” he wrote, adding that he was “receiving excellent medical care” and that “FC Bayern and my personal support network are right by my side, helping me through this. ”With clearance from his neurological specialists, Musiala said it was his own decision to continue with his normal life and return to the activity that matters most to him. “With the medical clearance of the neurologists, I want to continue doing what helps my recovery the most: simply living my daily life and pursuing my passion for playing football,” he said.He added that he had taken responsibility for the decision and was feeling positive about his progress. “Overall, I feel very positive and am on the right track,” Musiala wrote, before turning his attention towards Bayern’s season and the possibility of continuing to compete for trophies with his team.“What helps me most on this journey is continuing to chase victories and titles with my team and with your amazing support,” he said.Musiala also asked supporters to respect his wish to keep the details of his condition private, limiting those discussions to his closest circle, the club and his medical experts.
Article Summary: Jamal Musiala has revealed that he has been diagnosed with ‘temporarily occurring, brief absence seizures’ after collapsing during two Bayern Munich friendlies within four days. The 23-year-old Germany international said the episodes are caused by a neurological dysfunction, are treatable and are currently being managed with specialist medical care. During both matches, he appeared disoriented before going down, with the incidents occurring while he was actively playing.

Article Title: India romp past South Africa to register biggest win in Women's Hockey World Cup history
Article Text:
Photo/Agencies

“Keep pushing and keep motivating each other!” Former India captain and goalkeeper Savita could be heard above the din, telling the India huddle exactly what needed to be done ahead of their World Cup match against South Africa.And they did just that. India romped to a 6-1 win in their second group game in Amstelveen on Tuesday — their biggest win in World Cup history.Knowing they needed a big win, Sjoerd Marijne’s side came out all guns blazing, looking for goals from the word go. However, it was South Africa who had the first shot on goal within minutes, and for a moment, it seemed things might not be as easy for India.But Bichu Devi Kharibam made a good save to settle India’s nerves, and after a few near misses, the onslaught began.Sunelita Toppo (11), Navneet Kaur (17), Sushila Chanu Pukhrambam (25), Deepika (38), Lalremsiami (44) and Sakshi Rana (45) scored the goals as India went top of Group D with four points. China, who beat England 4-2 in the other group game earlier, also have four points, but India have a better goal difference.Towards the end, South Africa did find the net when Kayla de Waal scored following a penalty corner, but by then India knew the job was done.All focus now moves to Thursday when India take on England. A win or a draw there will take them through to the next round, irrespective of what happens in the match between China and South Africa.Despite Tuesday’s big win, however, it wasn’t a great game from India’s point of view, particularly in the first half when they were sloppy at times. Too many mis-passes and poor first touches could have been costly and India were fortunate that South Africa did not take advantage of them.Speaking during the half-time break, Marijne told the broadcaster: “Of course, when you see the score, you can say we are happy with 3-0, but I think it can be more. And I expect more from the team as well.”“We’ve seen too many individual errors, and they have had some good opportunities. So that’s something we really need to do better. Hopefully, we can score some more goals. That would be great,” he added.In the end, they did score more goals in the third quarter before taking their foot off the pedal in the fourth, when South Africa finally got a breakthrough of their own.The India players, meanwhile, were particularly good inside the D with their short passing. Both their opener and Deepika’s goal came from such moves. Navneet also continued her good showing, as did Neha, and Navneet was more than pleased with six different players finding the net.“If you see, six of our players scored goals, so it’s nice and feels good. Everyone in our team can score, and that’s good for us,” Navneet said after the game.Six different players getting on the scoresheet was perhaps the clearest reflection of the togetherness Marijne has been demanding from his side. The red-and-yellow ‘unity bands’ that every player and support staff member has been wearing around their wrists for the World Cup are meant to represent that spirit.On Tuesday, India showed that unity on the pitch as well.Yet the first-half performance also showed why Marijne wants more from his team. Against England on Thursday, India will need not just the goals but also greater control, discipline and precision if they are to take the next step in their World Cup campaign.
Article Summary: India beat South Africa 6-1 in their second World Cup game on Tuesday. Sunelita Toppo, Navneet Kaur, Sushila Chanu Pukhrambam, Deepika, Lalremsiami and Sakshi Rana scored the goals. Sjoerd Marijne's side go top of Group D with four points.

Article Title: Throwback: When Khabib Nurmagomedov put his UFC lightweight title on Islam Makhachev’s table with 3 powerful words: “future UFC champ”

Islam Makhachev is now a UFC champion across two weight divisions. He has also broken the promotion’s record for consecutive wins. But years before Makhachev reached the top, Khabib Nurmagomedov appeared to know exactly where his teammate was heading. A viral throwback moment from 2019 has brought that prediction back into focus.During UFC 242 fight week in Abu Dhabi, Nurmagomedov walked up behind Makhachev during a media interaction. He placed his UFC lightweight championship belt on the table in front of him. Nurmagomedov then delivered a simple message that would later look remarkably accurate:Future UFC champ”.The memorable moment happened in September 2019, during one of the biggest weeks in Khabib Nurmagomedov’s career. The undefeated Dagestani champion was preparing to defend his lightweight title against Dustin Poirier at UFC 242.Makhachev was also competing on the same card. He faced Davi Ramos and won the fight by unanimous decision.At the time, Makhachev was still viewed as a rising contender. He had not yet become the dominant champion that fans know today.That made Nurmagomedov’s gesture even more interesting.While Makhachev was speaking to reporters, Khabib Nurmagomedov approached him from behind.He placed his championship belt on the table and called his close friend and training partner the “Future UFC champ.”Makhachev appeared visibly humbled by the moment. He smiled and thanked Khabib.The prediction was not simply a random compliment.Nurmagomedov and Makhachev had grown up around the same fighting system created by their late coach, Abdulmanap Nurmagomedov. They trained together for years and became close friends.Nurmagomedov eventually became one of the greatest fighters in UFC history. He retired undefeated with a 29-0 professional record.Makhachev then followed a similar path.He won the vacant UFC lightweight championship at UFC 280 in 2022. He submitted Charles Oliveira to claim the title and later defended it four times.The throwback clip now carries even more weight because Makhachev has gone beyond the prediction.He eventually moved to welterweight and captured a second UFC championship by defeating Jack Della Maddalena. He then defended the welterweight title against Ian Machado Garry at UFC 330.That victory also pushed Makhachev’s UFC winning streak to 17 fights. He moved past Anderson Silva’s previous record of 16 consecutive UFC victories.Khabib celebrated the achievement on social media. In the post caption he wrote, “There is a word : Achievement. In sport it has a great significance, Islam and the word Achievement are synonyms)))) he achieved great heights in this sport, broke the record of series wins in UFC history, and is rightfully one of the best athletes to ever enter the octagon. May the Almighty keep you well, brother.”The 2019 moment therefore looks almost prophetic today. What began as a simple gesture from one friend to another became a remarkable prediction of what was to come.
Article Summary: Islam Makhachev is now a UFC champion across two weight divisions. He has also broken the promotion’s record for consecutive wins. Khabib Nurmagomedov appeared to know exactly where his teammate was heading. A viral throwback moment from 2019 has brought that prediction back into focus.

Article Title: Super Bowl LXI lands on Valentine’s Day for the first time in history creating an unusual football-versus-romance showdown
Article Text:
Super Bowl LXI (Getty Images)

Super Bowl LXI and Valentine’s Day create a unique clash

Super Bowl 2027 brings another major change for NFL fans

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Super Bowl LXI is about to create a very unusual sporting dilemma. The NFL ’s championship game is scheduled for February 14, 2027, putting it on Valentine’s Day for the first time in Super Bowl history. With romance and football competing for the same Sunday, fans have already begun joking about dinner reservations, watch parties and the ultimate relationship compromise.The date alone is enough to make the 2027 Super Bowl stand out. The game will take place at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, on February 14, meaning couples will have to decide how they want to spend one of the biggest nights on the American sporting calendar.For football fans, the answer may seem obvious. For couples with different priorities, however, the evening could require some negotiation.Social media has already embraced the idea. One Reddit commenter joked about the pressure on restaurants, writing:"The Valentine's Day brunch reservations are going to be harder to get than a Super Bowl ticket."Another post took the joke even further, imagining the holiday as a test of romantic loyalty:"Super Bowl on Valentine's? Peak relationship apocalypse incoming—guys choosing touchdowns over touchy-feely dates. Ladies, demand a halftime proposal or it's single season next year."The humor works because the conflict is so easy to imagine. A romantic dinner could overlap with pregame coverage. A reservation might clash with kickoff.And anyone hosting a Super Bowl party could suddenly find themselves planning around Valentine's Day expectations.There is also a convenient escape route. The game falls on Presidents' Day weekend, giving many people the chance to turn the occasion into a longer celebration. Couples could celebrate Valentine's Day on Saturday, watch the Super Bowl on Sunday and use Monday to recover from the late night.The unusual date is not the only reason Super Bowl LXI will be significant. ESPN will broadcast the championship game for the first time in network history, with ABC also carrying the event. ESPN has already outlined extensive programming and storytelling designed to build anticipation well before the game itself.The timing also feeds into a broader conversation about the Super Bowl calendar. The NFL has long faced calls to make the Monday after the championship game a national holiday, particularly because fans already tend to treat Presidents' Day weekend as a natural extension of Super Bowl celebrations.Commissioner Roger Goodell has previously discussed how changes to the NFL schedule could eventually push the Super Bowl toward Presidents' Day weekend. In comments cited in the original report, he said:"I think if you went to 18 weeks regular season that would probably occur," Goodell said at the time. "It is possible somewhere in the calendar. Could happen before that just because of the calendar, the way it lays out.But I think 18 weeks would get you to that point, and I think it would be a really great move."For now, February 14, 2027 remains a one-of-a-kind collision between football and romance. The NFL has confirmed the date, and fans have plenty of time to decide whether Super Bowl Sunday will be a date-night disaster, a couples' tradition or simply the perfect excuse to order wings and watch football together.
Article Summary: Super Bowl LXI is scheduled for February 14, 2027, putting it on Valentine's Day for the first time in Super Bowl history. The game will take place at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, on February 14. The NFL has long faced calls to make the Monday after the championship game a national holiday.

Brock Lesnar and Ric Flair are two of the biggest names in professional wrestling. But they have had very different experiences in terms of money. Lesnar was a crossover combat-sports star after excelling in amateur wrestling, WWE and the UFC, while Flair made his name over more than four decades in WCW and WWE.But there is a big gap, and public net-worth numbers are best seen as estimates, not audited financial statements. Lesnar’s contracts in the modern era, UFC purses and limited-appearance model allowed him to make individual paydays that were much larger than what was generally available to wrestlers during Flair’s peak years. Meanwhile, Flair continues to earn from his name, appearances, licensing and wrestling-related projects, despite the financial difficulties that have beset his wealth over the years.Brock Lesnar seems to be in a better financial state at the moment. Celebrity Net Worth estimates his net worth at $10 million, whereas NDTV reported an estimate of $17 million in June 2026. Other outlets have published higher numbers, a testament to the uncertainties that come with calculating celebrity net worth.Ric Flair is worth much less. His net worth has been estimated to be $500,000 by Celebrity Net Worth, but other estimates online have put the figure at a much higher number.The variation reflects the absence of publicly verified personal financial records, and the challenge of calculating assets, liabilities, royalties and ongoing income for a longtime entertainer.Lesnar’s wealth is intrinsically tied to his ability to command top dollar. He was an instant star in WWE after debuting in 2002, but he later moved away from the wrestling world to try his hand at the NFL and mixed martial arts before returning to WWE as an established crossover star.Lesnar’s career in WWE has been as much about scarcity as it has been about star power. He was often employed on a limited schedule around major storylines and premium live events for most of his later career instead of working weekly.Lesnar’s UFC career distinguished his money story from most WWE stars. After leaving professional wrestling, he came into MMA and immediately became a big draw. Beating Randy Couture for the heavyweight championship at UFC 91 made him a legit heavyweight champion and gave him a serious bump in commercial appeal.Lesnar has also earned money from endorsements and appearances. Jimmy John’s and other commercial deals are among his previous endorsement deals, and his celebrity status has helped his value outside the ring.He has also kept his lifestyle very private. Recent reports have pointed out that he prefers a rural lifestyle and owning vast amounts of land, rather than the high-profile celebrity lifestyle that many sports stars enjoy.Ric Flair’s financial story started in an era when the economics of professional wrestling were very different. The Nature Boy became one of the defining stars of the National Wrestling Alliance, World Championship Wrestling and WWE, headlining big events and winning championships through a career that spanned several decades.Flair made a ton of money in his time with WCW. One published estimate puts his WCW earnings from 1996-2000 at about $1.95 million. But the size of his earnings did not translate directly into lasting wealth because of taxes, legal obligations, medical expenses and other financial pressures.He also made a lot of money from his WWE career. Flair was a wrestler, manager and personality and stayed a close associate of the company for years. In 2005, during a divorce hearing, it was revealed that his annual WWE salary was reportedly around $500,000, showing how much he could make from wrestling even later in his career.Of the two stars, Flair's financial history is the starkest contrast. Celebrity Net Worth states that in 2000, the IRS filed a lien of more than $870,000 against him, and his further tax problems damaged his finances. The same source reports that in 2019 there was a major medical emergency that resulted in a medical bill of approximately $1.8 million.These pressures help explain why lifetime earnings and current net worth can look so dramatically different. Making millions in a career doesn’t always translate to keeping millions after taxes, debts, medical expenses and other costs.Lesnar’s future financial prospects will probably continue to be linked to his standing as a top-tier combat sports attraction. As his active wrestling career is changing, his name still has value for special appearances, merchandise, licensing and media projects.Flair’s earning model is a unique one. At 77, his money-making opportunities are increasingly linked to his legacy rather than regular ring competition. He still turns up at wrestling events, signs autographs and does other promotional stuff.Lesnar has a path to victory in the modern economics of sports and one of the rare WWE-to-UFC crossover careers. Flair’s financial legacy isn’t so much the wealth he has today, but the incredible value he brought to pro wrestling in terms of sales. Their careers demonstrate two different paths a wrestling superstar can take to earn money: Lesnar with premium modern contracts and crossover sports earnings, and Flair with longevity, character, championships and lasting brand recognition.
Article Summary: Brock Lesnar and Ric Flair are two of the biggest names in professional wrestling. But they have had very different experiences in terms of money. Lesnar was a crossover combat-sports star after excelling in amateur wrestling, WWE and the UFC. Flair made his name over more than four decades in WCW and WWE.

Article Title: “I just want to share that with all these little kids”: How Sophie Cunningham's $10,182 act of kindness turned WNBA frustration into a heartwarming moment for families in need
Article Text:
How Sophie Cunningham's $10,182 act of kindness turned WNBA frustration into a heartwarming moment for families in need(Getty)

Sophie Cunningham turned her WNBA fines joke into a $10,182 act of kindness

Sophie Cunninghum past Ronald McDonald House connection goes back to 2015

Sophie Cunningham had plenty of reasons to be frustrated in 2025. The Indiana Fever guard picked up multiple WNBA fines before a knee injury ended her season early. But a joke she made during that stretch took an unexpected turn. What started as a GoFundMe for fines or even a yacht raised $10,182. Cunningham then chose to give the money to a cause that had already touched her life.On Oct. 2, 2025, Sophie Cunningham launched a GoFundMe with a $26,000 goal. The Indiana Fever guard kept things playful when she explained the reason behind it.“This is more of a joke than anything. For fines only or to charity or for a yacht idk…,” Cunningham wrote on the GoFundMe page.The joke quickly caught on with her supporters. Over the next five days, 171 people donated to the fundraiser. Contributions ranged from $5 to $2,699, and the total eventually reached $10,182.That was when Cunningham decided the money would take a different path. “A yacht would be nice, but whatever we raise here will be going directly to Ronald McDonald House Charities. I’ll take care of my own fines. Y’all are the best,” Cunningham wrote in an update on the GoFundMe page, according to the Indianapolis Star's Oct.10, 2025 report.The decision came after a season in which Cunningham had become increasingly vocal about her frustrations with the WNBA. She had received multiple fines after speaking publicly about league officiating.In an August episode of her podcast, Show Me Something, Sophie Cunningham explained her disciplinary record with a joke of her own.“I’m officially 3-for-3 on being fined by the WNBA,” she said during the episode.She also explained why she continued to speak out, saying, “I promise you, everyone in our league feels that way and I’m just kind of the only one who says something.”So the fundraiser made sense at the moment. Sophie Cunningham had joked about the fines, fans responded and the money started coming in. Yet when she had more than $10,000 sitting in the fundraiser, she did not use it to erase the fines that had inspired the idea.Instead, she picked Ronald McDonald House Charities. That choice also came during a difficult personal stretch. Cunningham's 2025 season ended on Aug. 17 after she tore the MCL in her right knee. She later spent time on the sideline alongside several injured Fever teammates, including Caitlin Clark and Sydney Colson.During the Fever's exit interviews, Cunningham made it clear that she planned to return strong. When reporters asked whether she expected to be healthy for the 2026 season, she answered, “Hell yeah, man,” before saying she hoped to ramp up basketball activities in January.The fundraiser gave Cunningham a chance to do something positive while she waited for her own return.The charity was not just any random act. Sophie Cunningham first encountered Ronald McDonald House Charities as a teenager.Ronald McDonald House Charities helps families stay close to their children while they receive medical treatment. Its programmes provide places to stay, meals and other support for families facing difficult medical situations. Cunningham’s donation therefore went toward a cause that helps families during some of the hardest moments of their lives.On 2015, the Columbia Missourian reported on Cunningham's visit to a Ronald McDonald House in Chicago while she prepared for the McDonald's All-American Game. She met Brian and Jennifer Godish and their four-year-old son, Bradley, who had leukemia. Cunningham played with Bradley, built wooden train tracks with him and joined other children for basketball. She also volunteered to visit children who could not leave the hospital.“It makes me smile because this is how my parents raised me, and I’m just a little bit of who they are. I just want to share that with all these little kids and their parents,” Cunningham told the Columbia Missourian during that 2015 visit.Ten years later, she was once again giving to the same organisation. This time, her fans helped her raise the money.What began as a joke about WNBA fines ended with Sophie Cunningham choosing kindness over keeping the money for herself, adding a meaningful chapter to a connection that started long before her Indiana Fever career.
Article Summary: Sophie Cunningham started a GoFundMe page to raise money for fines or a yacht. The Indiana Fever guard then chose to give the money to Ronald McDonald House Charities. Cunningham first encountered the charity as a teenager during a McDonald's All-American Game.

Article Title: Can Nico Daws become the New Jersey Devils’ No. 1 goalie? Martin Brodeur believes he deserves the chance

Can Nico Daws beat Jake Allen and David Rittich for the Devils’ No. 1 goalie spot?

The New Jersey Devils will enter the 2026-27 season without a clear No. 1 goaltender, but Hall-of-Fame goalie Martin Brodeur believes Nico Daws deserves a real chance to take the job. After moving Jacob Markstrom to the Florida Panthers, New Jersey has left the door open for a new starter to emerge.Jake Allen and David Rittich are also in the mix, but Daws could have the biggest opportunity of his young NHL career. Brodeur, who serves as the Devils’ executive vice president of hockey operations, believes the 25-year-old deserves an opportunity to show what he can do in the NHL.According to Brodeur, the Devils are comfortable letting their goaltenders compete for the starting job rather than naming a clear No. 1 before the season begins. “The best starter is going to get the net,” Brodeur told The Hockey News. “I don't think there's a clear-cut No. 1 goalie in net.”That gives Daws a real opening. The 2020 third-round pick has spent much of his career moving between the NHL and AHL, and Brodeur believes the Devils have not given him enough chances to show what he can do.“Nico Daws is a kid who needs a chance,” Brodeur said. “We've been developing him for four years.We didn't put great teams in front of him in Utica and obviously his development slowed down because of that. But we need to give him a chance to see what we have.”While Daws has limited NHL experience, he has already delivered one performance that stands out. In the Stadium Series game against the Philadelphia Flyers at MetLife Stadium, he stopped 51 shots. Brodeur still remembers that performance when discussing Daws’ potential.“We put him into the Stadium Series game at MetLife Stadium in front of 70,000 people and he had 51 saves against the Flyers. He's got it, I really believe in him, we just never gave him a chance,” Brodeur said.That belief could be important for Daws as he competes with Allen and Rittich. Allen brings much more NHL experience, while Rittich has also spent years in the league. But neither has been locked into a heavy workload in recent seasons.Brodeur acknowledged that Markstrom will be missed but believes the current group can give New Jersey what it needs.“Jake showed us a lot last year when he had to play. He played some solid minutes for us,” Brodeur said. “We feel that both goalies are able to play.”If Daws can make the most of his opportunity, he could quickly move from an inexperienced option to the Devils’ top goalie. Brodeur has made his belief clear. Now Daws has the chance to prove it on the ice.
Article Summary: The New Jersey Devils have left the door open for a new No. 1 goalie. Hall-of- Fame goalie Martin Brodeur believes Nico Daws deserves a chance to take the job. Jake Allen and David Rittich are also in the mix, but Daws has the biggest opportunity.

Article Title: Inspiring story on motherhood by Naomi Osaka: “Taking care of myself is part of taking care of my daughter”- Tennis star reveals how self-care changed her approach to parenting
Article Text:
Inspiring story on motherhood by Naomi Osaka: “Taking care of myself is part of taking care of my daughter”- Tennis star reveals how self-care changed her approach to parenting

What did Naomi Osaka mean when she said self-care is part of motherhood ?

How did becoming a mother change Naomi Osaka’s view of tennis?

Why are boundaries so important to Osaka as a mother?

What can mothers learn from Naomi Osaka’s mental-health journey?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For Naomi Osaka, becoming a mother did not mean putting her own needs aside. Instead, it changed the way she thinks about self-care, mental health and life. The four-time Grand Slam champion, who has been open about her struggles with anxiety and pressure, has shared a simple but powerful message: “Taking care of myself is part of taking care of my daughter. ” Her words show why looking after yourself can also be an important part of being a good mother.Osaka became a mother in July 2023 when she welcomed her daughter, Shai, with rapper Cordae. Her journey into motherhood came during a major change in her life. She had stepped away from tennis for more than a year and was also trying to understand what she wanted from her career and her life.For Osaka, self-care is not about putting herself before her daughter. It is about making sure she is in a good place so she can also be there for her child.In her conversations about motherhood and mental health, Osaka has spoken about setting boundaries, taking time for herself and paying attention to what she needs. That can mean taking a quiet moment, meditating, getting enough rest when possible or simply saying no when something feels like too much.Her message also pushes back against the idea that mothers must always put themselves last.Being a mother does not mean a woman has to ignore her own feelings, needs or identity.Osaka’s approach is simple. A mother can love her child deeply and still need time for herself. In fact, taking care of her own mental and emotional health can help her be more present for her child.Tennis had been a huge part of Osaka’s life for years. She became world No. 1 and won four Grand Slam singles titles, including the US Open in 2018 and the Australian Open in 2019, 2021 and 2022.But success also came with pressure. Osaka made headlines in 2021 when she withdrew from the French Open after explaining that media duties were affecting her mental health. She later stepped away from tennis for an extended period.Becoming a mother gave her another chance to look at her life from a different point of view.Osaka returned to professional tennis in January 2024 after giving birth. The comeback was not easy. She had to rebuild her body, return to the demands of professional sport and deal with the normal ups and downs of competition.But motherhood also helped her understand that tennis was only one part of who she was.Winning was still important to her, but it was no longer the only thing that defined her. She could be a tennis player, a mother and her own person at the same time.That change in thinking also helped Osaka become more open about her emotions. Instead of feeling that she always had to appear strong, she became more comfortable talking about difficult moments and asking for support.Osaka has spent much of her career in the public eye. Her matches, interviews and personal life have all received huge attention. That level of attention can be difficult for anyone, and motherhood has given her even more reason to protect her private life and mental space.She has spoken about how hard it once was for her to say no because she worried about disappointing people. Over time, she learned that she could not make everyone happy and did not have to accept every demand placed on her.That lesson became an important part of how she approaches motherhood.For Osaka, boundaries can mean choosing when to work, taking time away from social media, protecting family time or simply refusing to take on something that could leave her overwhelmed.These choices are not about shutting people out. They are about knowing when she needs to step back.Her experience also sends an important message to other mothers. Saying no does not mean you care less. Taking a break does not mean you are lazy. Asking someone for help does not mean you have failed.Sometimes, protecting your own peace is what allows you to give more of yourself to the people you love.Perhaps the biggest lesson from Osaka’s story is that mental health should not be treated as something people have to hide.She has spoken openly about anxiety, pressure and the challenges that came with being a top athlete. She has also talked about wanting her daughter to grow up in an environment where talking about feelings is normal.Osaka has encouraged the idea that children should be able to express themselves, ask for help and understand their emotions. She has also talked about simple habits such as meditation, quiet time and spending meaningful time with family.For her, these lessons are not only things she can tell her daughter. They are things she can show her through her own actions.When a mother rests when she needs to, she shows her child that rest is important. When she talks about her feelings, she shows that emotions are normal. When she asks for help, she teaches her child that nobody has to deal with everything alone.That may be one of the most important parts of Osaka’s message.Motherhood does not have to mean losing yourself. A woman can still have dreams, a career, friendships, personal goals and time for herself while being a loving and devoted mother.Osaka’s journey shows that self-care is not about choosing yourself instead of your child. It is about making sure you are also cared for.For the tennis star, that balance has become part of the mother she wants to be. Her words, “Taking care of myself is part of taking care of my daughter,” capture that idea in the simplest way. Taking care of yourself is not taking love away from your child. Sometimes, it is what helps you give that love with more patience, energy and presence.
Article Summary: Tennis star Naomi Osaka reveals how self-care changed her approach to parenting. Osaka became a mother in July 2023 when she welcomed her daughter, Shai. The four-time Grand Slam champion has been open about her struggles with anxiety and pressure.

Mojang is keeping the content pipeline flowing in Minecraft, and the excitement amongst the community is at an all-time high. The next major update is the Third Drop of 2026, and they have yet to reveal the official name for it.It is shaping up to be one of the cosiest and most exploration-friendly updates the game has received in recent memory. It will bring a lot of things, including a brand new biome, a new wood set, furniture blocks, and a brand new structure to discover.Below we have all the details you need to know about the Minecraft Third Drop 2026.The Third Drop 2026 is an upcoming game drop that features dappled forests, abandoned camps, the poplar wood set, wool slabs and stairs, cushions, straw beds, and concrete slabs and stairs.Mojang is testing all the features through the snapshots, and players have already been able to experience most of them.The headline addition of the Third Drop is an entirely new overworld biome. The dappled forest consists of poplar trees with orange, yellow, and red leaves, as well as dirt blocks covered with leaf litter, new red shrubs, and brown mushrooms. After the Chaos Cubed drop took players deep underground, it is a breath of fresh air to have a brand-new destination to discover on the surface.The addition of poplar trees also brings a new wood set, which is a warm grey colour when broken down into planks and slabs. The poplar wood set comes in red, orange, and yellow leaf colors, and poplar saplings can be sold by wandering traders. It is a beautiful addition to the game's palette that builders in particular are going to go absolutely wild for.Scattered through the dappled forest are abandoned camps. They are small structures built from wool stairs and featuring chests or barrels to loot, with a tent-like visual design that fits the woodland explorer fantasy the biome is clearly going for. Having a lootable point of interest in a forest biome gives survival players an actual reason to push into unfamiliar territory.Even better, some abandoned camps contain maps hidden inside their chests. These maps lead to other abandoned camps or various other types of structures in the Overworld, making exploration feel genuinely rewarding in a way that few Minecraft updates have managed before.The drop also brings wool stairs, wool slabs, and wool cushions. Cushions in particular give players a genuine seat block, and pairing them with straw beds gives interiors a soft, homey layer that Minecraft's blocky palette has always struggled to deliver without workarounds.Straw beds are a new bed variant that lets players sleep through the night without changing their spawn point. They can only be used once and will be destroyed after use, and cannot be used in the Nether or the End.It is an elegant solution for players who want to skip the night on long expeditions without permanently shifting their respawn location.Concrete slabs and stairs have also been added as part of the final batch of features from the third drop, rounding out a building-focused update that is sure to keep the community's creative side busy for months to come.The Third Drop 2026 will certainly be pretty exciting to see when it arrives.
